about: Short clips of real test videos, cut by stream copy so they keep their codecs, containers and colour tags, or re-encoded where a copy's timestamps would be wrong. `golden.py clips` makes them from these sources.

clips.name: videoq_src.mp4
clips.what: 4K HDR10 (PQ, P3) HEVC 10-bit, 120 fps, MP4: the reference for the VideoQ encodes

clips.name: videoq_4k_h265.mkv
clips.source: E:/Video encodings/VideoQ HDR10 4K H.265 CRF 22 medium.mkv

clips.name: videoq_1080p_h265.mkv
clips.source: E:/Video encodings/VideoQ HDR10 1080p H.265 CRF 22 medium.mkv

clips.name: videoq_1080p_vvc.mkv
clips.source: E:/Video encodings/VideoQ HDR10 1080p VVC QP 32 faster.mkv
clips.what: 1080p VVC 10-bit HDR10: software decoding. Re-encoded as its source was (QP 32, faster), not copied: copied, its packets lose their timestamps (pts 0, then 1 over and over, with FFmpeg 9.0.1), which the app's decoders refuse, and FFmpeg decodes it instead. Its frames are timed N/120 s, so that all of them are kept: the source's first ones are timed before its container's start

clips.name: honeybee_src.mkv
clips.what: 4K SDR HEVC 8-bit with no colour tags: the reference for the HoneyBee encodes. Re-encoded (CRF 16), not copied: the source is a raw stream with B-frames, which cannot be copied into a container with right timestamps; its frames are timed N/120 s

clips.name: honeybee_h264.mkv
clips.what: 4K H.264 10-bit, no colour tags: software decoding, a bit depth other than the reference's
